Hon'ble Alok Mahra, J.
Mr. Lalit Sharma and Mr. Dheeraj
Joshi, learned counsel for the
applicant.
2. Mr. Rakesh Joshi and Mr. Prabhat
Kandpal, learned A.G.A. along with Mr.
Chitrarth Kandpal, learned Brief Holder
for the State.
3. This first bail application has been
moved by the applicant seeking regular
bail in F.I.R./ Case Crime No.77 of
2026, under Section 318(4), 336(3),
338, 340(2), 351(3), 352 & 61(2) of
B.N.S., 2023, registered at Police
Station Sahaspur, District Dehradun.
4. Heard learned counsel for the
parties and perused the material
available on record.
5. Learned counsel for the applicant
submits that the applicant has been
falsely implicated in the present case
and has no criminal antecedents. It is
further submitted that the applicant
has been in judicial custody since
06.08.2026. Learned counsel contends
that, even if the allegations levelled in
the F.I.R. are taken at their face value,
no offence is made out against the

UKHC010174412026
2026:UHC:9575
applicant. It is argued that the dispute,
if any, primarily relates to the
identification and demarcation of the
boundaries of the land purchased by
the complainant from the applicant and
other co-sharers. Learned counsel
further submits that the execution of
two registered sale deeds by the
applicant and the other co-sharers in
favour of the complainant is not in
dispute and that the said sale deeds
specifically recite that possession of the
land had been handed over to the
complainant. It is also contended that
the applicant and the other co-sharers
were recorded as Bhumidhar of Class I
in respect of the land in question and,
therefore, were competent to execute
the sale deeds. Learned counsel further
submits that the dispute, in essence, is
civil in nature, arising out of a land
transaction and a dispute regarding the
identification and demarcation of the
land conveyed, which has been given a
criminal colour by setting the criminal
law in motion. On these grounds,
learned counsel prays that the
applicant be enlarged on bail.
6. Learned State Counsel vehemently
opposed the bail application.
7. Having considered the
submissions advanced by learned
counsel for the parties and having
perused the material available on
record, this Court finds that the
applicant asserts that the transaction
in question was founded upon two
registered sale deeds executed in favour
of the complainant and that the dispute
essentially pertains to the identification

UKHC010174412026
2026:UHC:9575
and demarcation of the land conveyed
thereunder. The recitals in the sale
deeds regarding the transfer of
possession, as relied upon by learned
counsel for the applicant, are also
relevant considerations at this stage.
The applicant further claims to have
been recorded as a Bhumidhar of Class
I along with the other co-sharers. These
circumstances, when considered
cumulatively, warrant consideration of
the applicant's prayer for bail. The
applicant has no criminal antecedents
and has been in judicial custody since
06.08.2026. Having regard to the
nature of the dispute, the
circumstances brought on record and
the period of incarceration undergone
by the applicant, this Court is of the
view that the applicant's further
detention is not warranted at this
stage.
9. Accordingly, without expressing
any opinion on the ultimate merits of
the matter, this Court is of the
considered view that the applicant has
made out a case for grant of bail at this
stage. The bail application is allowed.
10. Let the applicant be released on
bail, on executing personal bond and
furnishing two reliable sureties, each of
like amount, to the satisfaction of Court
concerned.
 (Alok Mahra, J.)
 16.10.2026
Mamta
